tools.name: security_bitwarden
tools.description: Bitwarden password manager through its own MCP server (github.com/bitwarden/mcp-server), cloned on first use into ~/.usemcpkit/repos/security/bitwarden, built there and run locally: vault items, folders, attachments, Send, password and TOTP tools. Needs git, Node.js and npm on PATH, the Bitwarden CLI (`bw`) for the vault tools, and a vault unlocked with its `unlock` tool (a native password dialog; BW_SESSION, BW_CLIENT_ID and BW_CLIENT_SECRET from the client's env are passed along when set). It reads and changes real credentials, so allow only the tools you trust.. This is a SECTION of usemcpkit, not a callable tool. Call it with no arguments to open it: it lists its groups (each one another section) or, when it has none, loads its tools into the tool list.

tools.name: communication_medium
tools.description: Medium's API (api.medium.com/v1), which Medium has archived and no longer supports: it needs an integration token you already have, since Medium stopped issuing new ones. The API cannot read, edit or delete posts. Tools are named '<group>:<resource>:<action>'. `posts:posts:create_*` publishes under the token owner's name, so prefer publishStatus draft.. tools.description: Microsoft Teams through the community MCP server by Inditex (github.com/InditexTech/mcp-teams-server), cloned on first use into ~/.usemcpkit/repos/communication/teams, set up with uv and run locally on a Python that uv installs for it (the system Python is never used).
